metadata.methods_description: Seated participants reached with the right arm toward a target when a light turned on, then returned the hand to the right leg. EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz with a Brain Products actiCHamp 128-channel active electrode system (reference FCz, ground Fpz), together with 11 EMG channels. Each participant completed 3 runs of about 30 trials, covering three movement types and three assistance levels.

citation_details.abstract: This work presents a multimodal dataset containing synchronized electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and kinematic recordings acquired during wrist motor tasks performed with a three degree of freedom robotic exoskeleton (BiomechWrist) coupled to a virtual interface. The exoskeleton operated in transparent mode (actuators de-energized) to capture voluntary movements through high resolution encoders. citation_details.abstract: Abstract Background Muscle synergy analysis is a relevant approach to characterize motor control in different contexts, including the use of rehabilitative devices. Pilot studies on healthy individuals allow to derive baseline reference synergies to tailor the interventions and assess their effects in patient populations, but challenging levels of inter-subject variability are often reported. citation_details.author: Tipu Sultan, Kody Cool, Guangping Liu, Gajapriya Tamilselvan, Madi Babaiasl
citation_details.venue: 2022 9th IEEE RAS/EMBS International Conference for Biomedical Robotics and Biomechatronics (BioRob)
citation_details.abstract: Safe intent recognition for assistive robots remains challenging when integrating neural, muscular, and gaze signals, particularly under sensor degradation or failure. We propose TriSaFe-Trans, a lightweight tri-modal transformer that fuses electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and eye-tracking (ET) data via modality-specific temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) and bidirectional gated recurrent units (BiGRUs), combined with reliability-gated cross-modal attention. The model is trained using multi-objective selfsupervised pretraining, followed by supervised fine-tuning, to simultaneously decode action (REST vs. ACTION) and task (rest plus five assistive tasks) from fixed-length windows. citation_details.title: High-Density EEG and Multi-Muscle EMG Dataset during Object Prehension with a sensorized Grasping Box in Humans
citation_details.author: G. Lomele, T. Lencioni, S. D’Ambrosio, A. Comanducci, F. Lucchetti, A. Marzegan, C. Derchi, Stefano Garzonio, T. Atzori, M. Rabuffetti, P. Castiglioni, M. Ferrarin, L. Fornia
citation_details.abstract: Understanding how cortical areas control prehension movements requires synchronized neural and muscular data. For this aim, we introduce a novel open-access dataset of synchronized EEG and EMG recordings during prehension movements. The dataset combines high-density EEG (64 channels) with EMG recordings from 13 upper-limb muscles collected during prehension movements associated with 3 grip types: precision grip (thumb-index, PG), whole-hand power grasp (WH), and an unconventional grip (thumb-ring finger, UG). Data were acquired from 14 healthy participants performing visually guided prehension using a custom sensorized device that precisely timestamps action events, including go signals, object contacts, and lift completions. citation_details.author: Tipu Sultan, Param Sangani, Kody Cool, Pascal Sikorski, Guang-Ping Liu, H. Akbarpour, Madi Babaiasl
citation_details.abstract: We present NeuroCommitSSM, a decision-centric framework that models when to execute, not just what to do, for safe commit-to-execute control in assistive robotic manipulation. NeuroCommitSSM predicts a continuous commit-readiness score c_t in [0,1] from synchronized electroencephalography (EEG), electromyography (EMG), and eye-tracking (ET), and converts it into discrete commit events through dwell and hysteresis filtering. citation_details.title: A perspective on neuromechanical biomarkers for neurorehabilitation: towards reliable assessment in research and clinical practice
citation_details.author: Florencia Garro, Indya Ceroni, Andrea d’Avella, Marta Gandolla, E. Guanziroli, N. Irastorza-Landa, A. Ramos-Murguialday, D. Torricelli, M. Semprini
citation_details.abstract: Effective neurorehabilitation necessitates a reliable assessment of the patient’s sensorimotor status. Such assessment guides clinical decision-making and supports the evaluation of novel interventions. Yet, despite technological progress, it remains limited to clinical scales that are mostly based on subjective scoring systems and measurement protocols with poor reproducibility. Research on neuromechanical biomarkers—metrics of movement derived from kinematic, kinetic and physiological data—has demonstrated significant potential to advance towards more reliable assessment. However, their clinical validation and practical adoption remain limited, impeding the development of more objective, standardized, and clinically relevant measurement of movement. citation_details.title: BrainMergeEEG: An Open EEG Microstate Dataset for Studying Developers’ Brain Network Dynamics
citation_details.author: Robson Keemps, Kleinner Farias, Willian Bolzan, Rafael Kunst
citation_details.abstract: Although cognitive neuroscience and neuro-software engineering have advanced, there remains a lack of publicly accessible neural datasets that capture brain activity during complex tasks, such as the merging of refactored source code. This limitation undermines reproducibility and hinders the development of cognitively aware tools for high-cognitive-load scenarios. We introduce BrainMergeEEG, the first open EEG microstate dataset collected during refactored code-merging tasks, a demanding activity in collaborative software development. Our dataset includes recordings from 42 participants who completed resting-state sessions and ran controlled source merge tasks, totaling about 8.0 GB of EEG data. Data are organized by task condition and behavioral performance. To promote transparency and reuse, we provide preprocessing scripts and a fully reproducible experimental pipeline.
